THE EXPERIMENT

Small brain.
Ambitious career change.

This pilot uses 96 recorded descending neurons and their 3,199 connections from the MaleCNS v1.0 fruit fly dataset. Those edges represent 85,785 measured synaptic contacts.

We extract a densely connected motor circuit around DNa02, DNg13, DNp09 and DNp01. Flight telemetry enters a simplified rate model. Neural activity becomes throttle, engine gimbal and attitude-jet commands.

What actually learns?

Reward-based evolution strategies adjust 27 output coefficients and 12 gain groups on existing circuit connections. Better batches update the checkpoint. There is no language model or scripted landing autopilot flying the rocket.

The initial lesson learns thrust in an upright descent. Ocean missions unlock all three controls. Training runs in a background worker on your device. Your trainee’s progress is saved locally; “Save brain” exports a checkpoint.

What this can tell us

This is a small connectome-derived controller with engineered sensor and motor interfaces, not a whole-fly emulation. The rate dynamics and reward rule are engineering choices. Successful landings demonstrate task learning in this model, not biological fidelity or an advantage over other networks.

The flight-school checkpoint was trained locally. Its evaluation record is included below.
